visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The scene opens with a close-up of a person's hands holding a blue box of Hokkaido scallops. The kitchen background is brightly lit with natural light. The box is manipulated to show its contents, and a plastic bag full of frozen scallops is pulled out. (2) Transitioning to a preparation step, several frozen scallops are placed onto a metal wire rack situated inside a white rectangular ceramic dish. The camera captures the frosty texture of the seafood and the clean, organized kitchen setting with wooden accents. (3) A second thawing method is demonstrated. Water is poured into a white dish, and a small wooden bowl containing salt is emptied into it. A white spatula is used to stir the mixture until the salt dissolves completely, emphasizing technical detail. (4) Frozen scallops are submerged in the salt water. After a period of time, a small metal strainer is used to lift a scallop, showing it has softened and slightly expanded. The background remains a tidy, domestic kitchen area. (5) The scallops are placed back on a rack and a hand uses a white paper towel to meticulously pat them dry. This phase highlights the importance of surface moisture removal for achieving a proper sear during the subsequent cooking stage. (6) A pink cast-iron skillet is placed on a white portable gas stove. A hand turns the control knob to ignite the flame. The pan's temperature is tested by hovering a hand above it and then flicking water onto the surface. (7) Scallops are placed into the hot, oiled pan using metal tongs. The camera focuses on the sizzling reaction as they hit the surface. They are flipped to reveal a deep golden-brown crust, demonstrating successful heat management and searing technique. (8) Excess oil is blotted from the pan using a paper towel held by tongs. A block of butter is added, melting rapidly and creating a frothy sauce. The scallops are basted and tossed in the butter to enhance flavor and color. (9) The final phase shows the cooked scallops arranged on a white plate. Pepper is ground over them, and a spoon drizzles pan juices. A fork presses the scallop to show elasticity, and a knife slices one to reveal the rare interior.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Logo]: @RosalinaKitchen. [Slogan]: 準備生食級的干貝. (2) [Slogan]: 生食級的干貝才可以吃五分熟喔!. (3) [Slogan]: 這個是S尺寸無論是煮湯還是乾煎都很恰當!. (4) [Slogan]: 解凍法一：準備一個網網把干貝放上來解凍解凍後，水會滴到盆子上干貝不會濕濕的. (5) [Slogan]: 蓋上蓋子，像這樣放在冰箱自然解凍一個晚上. (6) [Slogan]: 解凍法二：（鹽水快速解凍）盆子裡放入800ml冷水. (7) [Slogan]: 加入24克的鹽鹽的比例是水的3%. (8) [Slogan]: 攪拌至溶解.... (9) [Slogan]: 放入冷凍干貝只要放的下，幾顆都可以. (10) [Slogan]: 解凍的時間不得超過20分鐘. (11) [Slogan]: 泡得太久，干貝會太鹹，失去風味溫度也會過高. (12) [Slogan]: 解凍前略小一點. (13) [Slogan]: 解凍後，看起來會略大一點. (14) [Slogan]: 將解凍好的干貝用廚房紙巾擦乾水分. (15) [Slogan]: 不要灑鹽！要煎之前在擦乾一次！. (16) [Slogan]: 開中小火加熱（鑄鐵鍋煎法...）. (17) [Slogan]: 鑄鐵鍋可以先用奶油養過鍋會更不沾. (18) [Slogan]: 大約加熱3分鐘用手測試一下溫度.... (19) [Slogan]: 最好的方法就是用水測試快速蒸發 表示溫度到了！. (20) [Slogan]: 先關火30秒到1分鐘. (21) [Slogan]: 接著倒入橄欖油或者耐高溫的油.... (22) [Slogan]: 開中小火加熱....搖晃鍋子讓鍋子均勻的沾到油脂. (23) [Slogan]: 感覺油表面油油亮亮的，有光澤感溫度就差不多了！. (24) [Slogan]: 油在鍋子裡的流動是很滑順的. (25) [Slogan]: 這時後就可以把干貝放進來煎了.... (26) [Slogan]: 一次不要放很多鍋子的溫度會下降太快. (27) [Slogan]: 通通放進來之後，先翻動一下干貝減少沾黏狀況.... (28) [Slogan]: 接著繼續煎煎到表面產生焦香為止. (29) [Slogan]: 看一下焦香狀況. (30) [Slogan]: 差不多這樣微微焦香就可以翻面了. (31) [Slogan]: 現在用廚房紙巾把多餘的油都擦乾淨. (32) [Slogan]: 鍋子傾斜一邊讓油集中，擦乾淨！. (33) [Slogan]: 這些油都不要了. (34) [Slogan]: 干貝再翻面過來已經很有焦香囉！. (35) [Slogan]: 這時後轉小火或者把火關掉...放入15克的奶油. (36) [Slogan]: 奶油後放才會有奶香味！. (37) [Slogan]: 現在翻動干貝讓兩面都沾到鍋裡的焦香. (38) [Slogan]: 抹一抹，滾一滾干貝表面就會有更漂亮的焦香色～～❤❤. (39) [Slogan]: 你可以在這時後加新鮮百里香或者蒜末...味道會更讚❤❤. (40) [Slogan]: 起鍋後，灑點綜合胡椒或者放幾片檸檬味道很清新～. (41) [Slogan]: 沾一點鍋裡的奶油...干貝吃起來會很滑順. (42) [Slogan]: 像這樣～超好吃的『奶油煎干貝』就完成啦～❤. (43) [Slogan]: 你可以用擦子壓一下如果很有彈性，表示干貝5分鐘口感是相當柔軟好吃！❤. (44) [Slogan]: 切開來看一下～❤. (45) [Slogan]: 哇～～裡面是5~7分熟的狀態. (46) [Slogan]: 這是我覺得干貝最好吃的口感！❤. (47) [Slogan]: 如果干貝太熟，那口感就會比較硬不好吃喔！！. (48) [Slogan]: 更多美味料理請追蹤我 IG 臉書：蘿潔塔的廚房 YouTube: @RosalinaKitchen.
